correctness.rationale: Every base vertex is forced by domination and perfect-matching feasibility at its private leaves. At most one private leaf per root may be selected, and all remaining roots form exactly one perfectly matchable induced subset. Reversing these conditions proves a bijection; the multiplicity product counts distinct leaf choices rather than internal matchings. Without even cycles, each perfect support has a unique matching; positive edge weights give a monomer-dimer generating polynomial and Heilmann–Lieb gives strictly negative roots, yielding purely imaginary nonzero paired-domination roots. Boundary and normalization cases were checked. Independent direct enumeration of 3,401,516 candidate subsets on 2,174 graph-and-multiplicity instances passed; finite verification is not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The previously known scalar single-leaf minimum, PMS polynomial and matching real-root theorem are acknowledged. Materially distinct result is the arbitrary graph and heterogeneous pendant-leaf all-cardinality bijection together with the weighted matching and imaginary-axis conclusion for all no-even-cycle bases. Searches and primary material inspections did not identify an equivalent theorem; the simple uniform case is elementary, and the inaccessible 2016 paper and possible unindexed derivations remain substantive risks.

value.rationale: The theorem is a complete classification and weighted cardinality enumerator for arbitrary base graphs with arbitrary unequal positive private-leaf multiplicities. It preserves distinct perfect-matchable vertex supports rather than counting perfect matchings multiple times, which is essential on even-cycle bases, and yields a uniform root-location theorem for the infinite no-even-cycle class using weighted monomer-dimer stability. This supplies natural counting and zeros information beyond known minimum-cardinality facts; no paper-sized claim or unsupported downstream application is required.
